source_text: Nam postquam collectionem nostram, quae tanta est veritate munita, ut in te tota ferretur, nec convicio eam temerare quiveris, Deo adigente laudasti, effectum tamen eius accusas.
pass_a_gloss: For after our gathering, which is fortified with so great truth that it was wholly carried against you, you were not able to violate it even by insult, and, God compelling, you praised it, yet you accuse its effect.
pass_b_english: For my conclusion is fortified by such truth that its whole force falls upon you. Unable even to violate it with abuse, you praised it under God’s compulsion; yet you accuse the result to which it leads.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
